GridPulse-RESTORE

A scaled 24 V, 50 Hz distribution feeder network with STM32 protection and ESP32-supervised, human-approved service restoration, designed and simulated in Proteus 8.

Plant
24 Vrms / 50 Hz, three radial feeders, separate alternate source
Protection authority
STM32F103C8T6 with hardware trip latches
Gateway
ESP32. It forwards requests and never decides.
Restoration
Dead transfer, break-before-make, operator approval

Build status

The project is laid out as six schematic blocks on one A2 sheet. Two blocks are fully built in Proteus, one is partly built, and three are designed on paper and not yet drawn in Proteus. Nothing has been run as a full closed-loop simulation yet, so every fault current and trip time below is calculated, not measured.

■ Built■ Partly built■ Designed, not yet built

A1Source and earthing

Built
  • Primary source with near-source impedance Zs = 0.5 + j0.314 Ω (R 0.5 Ω, L 1 mH).
  • 1:1 transformer with a tapped secondary for voltage regulation.
  • Neutral earthing resistor (10 Ω) through an earth-current transformer with a 33 Ω burden, giving I_EARTH_P/N.
  • Main breaker as a 5 V relay with flyback diode, driven from CB_MAIN_DRV.
  • Surge clamp: two 1N4755A (43 V) zeners back to back.
  • Separate alternate source with its own tie breaker and a 60 Ω load, never paralleled with the primary.
  • Control power: two 24 V supplies diode-OR'd into an MC34063 buck (5.2 V) and an LM317 (3.3 V).

Left to do: fit the fifth tap switch (four are in), so the regulator has a true nominal tap.

A2Distribution network

Built
  • Three feeders, each behind a 5 V relay breaker (CB1–3_POWER) with flyback diode.
  • Each feeder is two line sections (1 Ω, 2 mH, 1 µF shunt) with a sectionaliser between them.
  • Fault points in both sections of every feeder, through 10 Ω to ground.
  • Loads: F1 48 Ω, F2 24 Ω + 57 mH with a switchable 33 µF power-factor capacitor, F3 bridge rectifier with 470 µF and 220 Ω.
  • A tie switch at each feeder end to the DG_TIE rail.
  • Three feedback relays (CBn_FB, 10 kΩ pull-down) mirroring each breaker coil.

Left to do: turn the sectionalisers and tie switches into relays with drivers, place an ACS712 current sensor in series after each breaker, and add the tie interlock through each breaker's contact.

B1Measurement and protection

Partly built
  • Bus and alternate-side voltage chains: 470 kΩ / 10 kΩ divider, MCP6002 buffer, 1 kΩ / 100 nF filter, diode clamps to the ADC.
  • One ACS712-05B current channel (feeder 1) with its filter capacitor.
  • Four comparator channels feeding a 74HC279 latch and 74HC04 inverters, giving TRIP_F1_N to TRIP_F4_N.
  • Peak-detector stage and the divider that sets the under- and over-voltage thresholds.

Left to do: the voltage-window comparators, the earth-fault amplifier, the zero-cross detector, and the ACS712 channels for F2, F3, the alternate tie and the main.

B2STM32 control core

Designed
  • STM32F103C8T6 with reset, boot, SWD and an 8 MHz clock.
  • Three 74HC595 outputs and three 74HC165 inputs on SPI2 for 24 outputs and 24 inputs.
  • ULN2803 relay drivers, gated by the hardware trip latches so no firmware sits in the trip path.
  • Tap sequencer, RS-485 Modbus read-only link, DS3231 clock, 24LC256 event log, watchdog.

Status: fully specified on the poster, with the pin plan below. Not yet drawn in Proteus.

C1ESP32 supervision

Designed
  • ESP32 gateway with Wi-Fi, MQTT and a framed UART link to the STM32.
  • Signed approval token (HMAC, nonce, 30 s lifetime) that the STM32 re-checks.
  • Mode selector (advisory, supervised, manual) and a local approve button.
  • Restoration time and reliability indices, labelled synthetic.

Status: designed. Not yet drawn in Proteus.

C2Test bench and security

Designed
  • Comms-impairment shim: drop, flaky and corrupt controls on the UART.
  • Load-step and surge injectors for testing regulation and the clamp.
  • Thirteen-test security and degradation matrix.
  • Optional sync check for a keyed generator-parallel mode.

Status: designed. Not yet drawn in Proteus.

The idea

When a fault trips a feeder, the healthy customers behind it can often be fed from another source. The hard part is doing that safely. GridPulse-RESTORE isolates the faulted feeder, checks that the alternate source can carry the extra load, waits for a human to approve, and then transfers the load without ever connecting two sources together.

The design follows a human-on-the-loop restoration approach: automation proposes, a person authorises, and the protection device keeps the final say. The ESP32 and the dashboard can only forward a request. The STM32 re-checks every condition before any relay moves.

Rules the design is built around

  1. The STM32 is the protection authority. The ESP32 only forwards requests and displays results.
  2. Break before make. A tie never closes while its feeder breaker is closed, and two sources are never paralleled.
  3. Hardware trips independently of firmware. Overcurrent latches pull the relay drivers low directly.
  4. Feedback confirms every move. A command is not trusted until the position feedback agrees.
  5. Safe defaults. Pull-downs and an output-disable pin keep every breaker open at reset or power loss.
  6. A failed or unknown check never actuates. Safe abstention is a valid outcome.

The fault section is identified from loop reactance, which does not depend on fault resistance: about 0.94 Ω means section 1, about 1.57 Ω means section 2. A section 1 fault is isolated and the load can be transferred. A section 2 fault leaves the load behind the fault, so transfer is refused and the state goes to BLOCKED.

Control core

The STM32F103C8T6 has 37 usable I/O pins. Three 74HC595 shift registers and three 74HC165 shift registers on SPI2 turn four pins into 24 outputs and 24 inputs.

ChipBits 0 to 7

Safe defaults: the shift-register output-enable pin has a pull-up and every driver input has a pull-down, so every breaker stays open at reset. Relay coils are 5 V, energise to close, and fall open when power is lost.

Restoration logic

State machine (11 states)
StateEntry conditionRequired action
BOOT_SELF_TESTReset or startupSafe outputs, self-test of sensors and feedback
NORMALInputs valid, no faultMonitor and publish status
FAULT_DETECTEDComparator or threshold crossedLatch the event, find the feeder, inhibit unsafe transfer
ISOLATINGTrip requestedOpen the feeder, start a timeout, watch feedback
ISOLATION_FAILEDFeedback does not confirm openBlock transfer and alarm
TRANSFER_ASSESSMENTIsolation confirmedCheck source, capacity, topology and measurements
WAIT_APPROVALTransfer is feasibleKeep the tie open, wait with a timeout, allow reject
TRANSFER_EXECUTIONApproval valid and recheckedBreak before make, verify feedback and V, I
RESTOREDTransfer verifiedLog success, watch for overload
BLOCKEDUnsafe or infeasibleKeep the path open, record the reason
COMMS_DEGRADEDESP32 or Wi-Fi unavailableLocal protection continues, remote status marked unavailable

Eligibility

A close action is allowed only if every term is true. Any failed or unknown term sets eligibility to zero.

TermIn this design
Data validBreaker feedback and current sensors sane
Data ageTelemetry newer than a set limit
No work blockWork-permit input for that feeder is open
ElectricalCapacity and voltage window pass
TopologyBreak before make, no paralleling
AuthoritySupervised mode with a valid token, or the local key

Reliability and restoration time

The ESP32 computes these from time-stamped STM32 events. Every figure is labelled synthetic: a bench simulation, not annual utility data.

T_rest = T_det + T_conf + T_iso + T_plan + T_cmd + T_ver SAIDI = Σ N_i U_i / N_T SAIFI = Σ N_i / N_T CAIDI = SAIDI / SAIFI ENS = Σ P_crit (1 − z) Δt

Time spent waiting for a human in WAIT_APPROVAL is logged separately, so restoration time is reported with and without it.

Security and degradation tests

The test bench injects link faults and bad commands, then checks that the STM32 refuses unsafe actions and keeps protecting locally. All thirteen tests are specified; none has been run yet.

IDInjectionExpected response

T8Work permit closedEligibility 0, BLOCKED, no switching
T9Breaker feedback wire openISOLATION_FAILED, no tie close

What is next

  1. Finish A1 and A2: fifth tap, relays for the sectionalisers and ties, ACS712 sensors, tie interlock.
  2. Finish B1: remaining current channels, voltage-window comparators, earth-fault amplifier, zero-cross.
  3. Draw B2, then C1 and C2, and bring up the firmware state machine.
  4. Run the staged tests: plant only, analogue, acquisition, protection, restoration, then the ESP32 link.
  5. Record the fault, isolation, approval and transfer sequence as evidence.

Design checks made along the way

  1. The clamp must be 43 V. A 36 V zener (1N4753A) conducts at the +5 % tap peak of 35.6 V.
  2. F3's resistor must be 220 Ω, not 33 Ω, so the feeder draws about 0.3 A as the capacity check assumes.
  3. Transfer is dead only. A synchronism check is kept for an optional keyed generator-parallel mode.
  4. Relay coils are 5 V and driven from the STM32. The ESP32 drives no relay.
  5. The main breaker has no hardware overcurrent latch because it cannot tell a feeder fault from a bus fault. It is protected by a time-graded firmware element and a hardware earth-fault trip.
  6. Bias reference, divider and peak-detector discharge all return to the buffered 1.65 V reference, not to ground.
Tools: Proteus 8 Professional, STM32F103C8T6, ESP32, ACS712, 74HC logic, MC34063. Voltage, current and timing figures in this write-up are calculated from the design values, not measured from a completed simulation.
